cabernet-sauvignon.definition: A highly regarded style of red wine that originated in Bordeaux, France.

merlot.definition: Black wine grape originally from the region of Bordeaux.

chardonnay.definition: Dry white table wine resembling Chablis but made from Chardonnay grapes.

pinot-noir.definition: A dark-skinned grape variety widely used in wine production.
pinot-noir.exampleUsage: The vineyard map identifies a block planted with Pinot Noir grapes.

sauvignon-blanc.definition: A green-skinned grape variety widely grown for wine production.
sauvignon-blanc.exampleUsage: The vineyard grows Sauvignon Blanc grapes in a separate block.

riesling.definition: White grape grown in Europe and California.

syrah.definition: A dark-skinned grape variety used in wine production and also known as Shiraz in some regions.
syrah.exampleUsage: The agricultural chart lists Syrah among red grape varieties.

malbec.definition: A dark-skinned grape variety associated especially with Argentina and parts of France.
malbec.exampleUsage: The vineyard guide identifies Malbec as a grape variety.

tempranillo.definition: A dark-skinned grape variety widely grown in Spain and Portugal.
tempranillo.exampleUsage: The viticulture lesson lists Tempranillo among Iberian grape varieties.

zinfandel.definition: Small black grape grown chiefly in California.

vine.definition: A climbing or trailing plant with a long thin stem.

trellis.definition: To train on a trellis, as of a vine.

row.definition: An arrangement of objects or people side by side in a line.

terroir.definition: A term for the combined environmental conditions of a growing place, such as soil, climate, slope, and local practices, that influence an agricultural product.
terroir.exampleUsage: The viticulture class discussed how soil and climate contribute to terroir.

irrigation.definition: Supplying dry land with water by means of ditches etc.

root-stock.definition: The rooted lower part of a plant onto which another variety is grafted.
root-stock.exampleUsage: The vine variety was grafted onto disease-resistant rootstock.

grafting.definition: The act of grafting something onto something else.

pruning.definition: Something that has been pruned off of a plant.

bud-break.definition: The stage in a plant's growth when dormant buds open and new shoots begin to emerge.
bud-break.exampleUsage: Bud break began after temperatures rose in spring.

flowering.definition: When a plant is in a state of possessing one or multiple flowers and/or blooms.

veraison.definition: The stage when grapes begin to ripen and change color.
veraison.exampleUsage: Veraison marks the beginning of visible ripening in the grapes.

harvest.definition: The gathering of crops when they are ready.

crush.definition: To compress with violence, out of natural shape or condition.

growing-season.definition: It is the period of the year when a crop has the best conditions for growth.

dormancy.definition: A state of quiet (but possibly temporary) inaction.

frost-protection.definition: Methods used in agriculture to reduce damage to plants from freezing temperatures.
frost-protection.exampleUsage: The vineyard manager monitored frost-protection systems during a cold night.

netting.definition: A net of transparent fabric with a loose open weave.

hand-picking.definition: Harvesting fruit or crops manually rather than with a machine.
hand-picking.exampleUsage: The harvest crew used hand-picking for selected grape bunches.

cellar-master.definition: A person responsible for managing a wine cellar and supervising storage or production operations.
cellar-master.exampleUsage: The cellar master maintained inventory records.

sommelier.definition: A waiter who manages wine service in a hotel or restaurant.

vineyard-manager.definition: A person responsible for planning and supervising the cultivation and maintenance of a vineyard.
vineyard-manager.exampleUsage: The vineyard manager checked the irrigation schedule.

winemaker.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Winemaker" in an educational description.

harvest-crew.definition: A group of workers who collect ripe crops during harvest.
harvest-crew.exampleUsage: The harvest crew began work early in the morning.

cooper.definition: United States industrialist who built the first American locomotive.

n-gociant.definition: A wine-industry merchant or business that buys grapes, juice, or wine from growers or producers and sells wine under its own name.
n-gociant.exampleUsage: The industry glossary defines a négociant as a wine merchant.
